key_insight: High-temperature alloy degradation is governed by diffusion-controlled oxidation, and performance depends on forming continuous protective scales such as α-Al2O3 or Cr2O3.
engineering_relevance: For turbines, power systems, and other hot-section components, coating design and alloy selection are the main levers to extend service life under temperatures above 1500°C.
method: Use thermodynamic and kinetic oxidation theory to predict scale growth.
Apply thermal spray, diffusion, or high-entropy alloy coatings to promote protective oxide formation.
Match alloy composition to critical Al or Cr levels for stable scale development.
evidence_signal: The review cites parabolic oxidation kinetics, activation energies from about 171 kJ/mol for Ti-based refractory alloys to higher values for alumina-forming systems, and composition thresholds of >5 wt.% Al or >20 wt.% Cr for continuous protective scales.
watch_item: Protective behavior is highly composition- and temperature-dependent, so coating adhesion, scale spallation, and non-protective oxide formation remain practical risks in service.
paper_title: High-Temperature Oxidation and Corrosion of Alloys: Kinetics, Scale Formation, and Protective Coatings
